title: Quasi-compactness descends along flat surjective quasi-compact morphisms (Stacks 02KQ)
statement: Let $g:S'\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] (the preimage of every affine open of $S$ is quasi-compact). Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and let $f':X\times_SS'\to S'$ be the second projection of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f'$ is quasi-compact, then $f$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KQ (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact, line 5471: 'The property P(f) = "f is quasi-compact" is fpqc local on the base'), the direction 'the base change has P => f has P' of Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310) for the one-member fpqc covering $\{g:S'\to S\}$. The one-member family $\{g\}$ is then an fpqc covering of $S$ (Topologies, Lemma Tag 03L7, lemma-recognize-fpqc-covering, topologies.tex line 2904, (2): for an affine open $U\subseteq S$ the open $g^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact and $g(g^{-1}(U))=U$)

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq S$ be an affine open. By the definition of a quasi-compact morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] it suffices to show that $f^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact. Since $g$ is quasi-compact, $V:=g^{-1}(U)\subseteq S'$ is a quasi-compact open of $S'$ (definition of quasi-compactness of $g$ applied to the affine open $U$). This is the source's reduction to an affine base (it reduces to $S$ affine by Zariski locality, Schemes 01K4; with the definition in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] the reduction is the definition itself).

source.place: Descent, Lemma 02KQ (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact), proof, lines 5481-5487 ('Being quasi-compact is Zariski local on the base ... let $S' \to S$ be a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes')

proof.text: Write $X'=X\times_SS'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$, so that $f\circ p=g\circ f'$. Since $f'$ is quasi-compact and $V$ is a quasi-compact open of $S'$, the open $W:=f'^{-1}(V)\subseteq X'$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open]. (In the source, with $S'$ affine, this is 'Then $X'$ is quasi-compact'.)

source.place: Descent, Lemma 02KQ (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact), proof, lines 5481-5487 ('Assume that the base change $f' : X' \to S'$ is quasi-compact. Then $X'$ is quasi-compact')

proof.text: The projection $p:X'=X\times_SS'\to X$ is surjective: it is the base change of the surjective morphism $g:S'\to S$ along $f:X\to S$ (identifying $X\times_SS'$ with $S'\times_SX$ by the canonical symmetry isomorphism of the fibre product, which is a homeomorphism commuting with the projections), so [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] applies with its $f,g$ taken to be $g,f$.

source.place: Descent, Lemma 02KQ (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact), proof, lines 5481-5487 ('and $X' \to X$ is surjective')

proof.text: $p(W)=f^{-1}(U)$. If $x'\in W$ then $f(p(x'))=g(f'(x'))\in g(V)\subseteq U$, so $p(x')\in f^{-1}(U)$. Conversely, let $x\in f^{-1}(U)$; by step 3 choose $x'\in X'$ with $p(x')=x$; then $g(f'(x'))=f(x)\in U$, so $f'(x')\in g^{-1}(U)=V$ and $x'\in f'^{-1}(V)=W$.

source.place: Descent, Lemma 02KQ (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact), proof, lines 5481-5487 ('Hence $X$ is quasi-compact', with $X$ replaced by $f^{-1}(U)$)

proof.text: The restriction $p|_W:W\to X$ is continuous (a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] is continuous on underlying spaces, and restriction to a subspace preserves continuity) and $W$ is quasi-compact (step 2), so its image $p(W)=f^{-1}(U)$ (step 4) is quasi-compact in the topology induced from $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact]. As $U$ was an arbitrary affine open of $S$, $f$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].
